advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the docstring of test_recanonicalization_converges_within_one_reemit with its assertions: the test asserts no emission on the first pass, not a re-emit-then-settle sequence.
evidence: docstring: "The first pass re-emits; once the landed form becomes the baseline the body is quiet, so the convergence costs one update rather than looping."
assertion: `assert "description" not in _run(_MD, recanonicalized, sent)` — asserts NO emission on the first pass
outbound_field_diff.py:50-54 `_text_matches` does `a.rstrip() == b.rstrip()` so `sent` vs `sent+"\n"` compare equal, making the pass quiet immediately (no re-emit occurs)
outbound_field_diff.py:362 `_suppressed_by_inbound("description", local_desc, normalized_local=fitted)` suppresses when the normalized local (==sent) matches baseline (==sent)
advisory.finding: The docstring of test_recanonicalization_converges_within_one_reemit describes a re-emit-then-converge sequence ('The first pass re-emits; once the landed form becomes the baseline the body is quiet'), but both assertions assert the body is ALREADY quiet with no emission — the first pass emits nothing because normalize_outbound(_MD) equals the baseline and _text_matches tolerates the trailing newline. The narrative contradicts the test's actual behavior.
advisory.suggested_fix: Reword the docstring to state that trailing-whitespace-only re-canonicalization is tolerated by the comparator so the pass is quiet immediately (no re-emit), rather than describing a one-shot re-emit that the test does not exercise.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive assertion to test_recanonicalization_converges_within_one_reemit that the first (non-converged) pass actually emits exactly one description update before the quiet passes, so the 'one re-emit' contract is exercised.
evidence: docstring: "A benign Jira re-canonicalization settles after one re-emit" / "The first pass re-emits; once the landed form becomes the baseline the body is quiet" (lines 134-138)

Neither assertion checks that a description IS emitted; both are negative, so the 'one re-emit'/'one update' behavior is never exercised — the test cannot distinguish 'converges in one re-emit' from 'never emits'.

The emit-then-converge contract IS asserted elsewhere (tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_echo_suppression.py:110 test_legacy_body_upgrades_once asserts both 'description' in first and convergence), showing the missing positive assertion is the norm.
advisory.finding: test_recanonicalization_converges_within_one_reemit asserts only that two passes are quiet ('description' not in changed) but never asserts the 're-emit' its name and docstring promise ('settles after one re-emit'; 'The first pass re-emits'). Both constructed passes have the local body already suppressed against the baseline, so the test verifies no-emit only; it would pass unchanged if the code emitted zero on every pass and therefore cannot detect a regression that drops the single re-emit it claims to pin.
advisory.suggested_fix: Precede the quiet-pass assertions with a case where the re-canonicalized form is genuinely not yet the baseline (e.g. baseline=None or a stale prior wire) and assert 'description' in that result and its value equals the rendered body, then assert the subsequent passes are quiet — mirroring test_legacy_body_upgrades_once.
